hierarchy.title: Rate hierarchy
hierarchy.body: Rates follow a three-level hierarchy: organisation defaults, matter overrides, and client overrides. A more specific rate always takes precedence. For example, a client-specific rate overrides the matter rate, which overrides the org default.

costVsBilling.title: Cost rates vs. billing rates
costVsBilling.body: Billing rates are what you charge your clients per hour. Cost rates represent your internal cost per team member — typically their salary or contractor rate divided by working hours. The difference between billing and cost rates drives your profitability metrics.

billableTime.title: Billable vs. non-billable time
billableTime.body: Billable time is work that can be charged to a client and appears on fee notes. Non-billable time — such as internal meetings, admin, or professional development — is tracked for effort visibility but is not billed.

currency.title: Currency settings
currency.body: Your organisation's currency applies to all rates, fee estimates, and fee notes. Choose the currency you bill your clients in. This setting affects display formatting across the platform.

snapshots.title: Rate snapshots
snapshots.body: When time is recorded or a fee note is generated, the current rate is captured as a snapshot. If you change a rate later, existing time recordings and fee notes retain their original rate. This ensures historical accuracy in your financial records.

types.title: Fee estimate types
types.body: A fixed fee estimate sets a capped monetary amount for the matter. Time and materials tracks hours worked against an estimated total. Choose fixed for predictable-cost matters and T&M for ongoing or variable-scope work.

alerts.title: Alert thresholds
alerts.body: Set percentage thresholds (e.g., 75%, 90%) to receive notifications when your matter's fee estimate reaches those levels. Alerts help you take action before a fee estimate is fully consumed.

vsActual.title: Fee estimate vs. actual
vsActual.body: This comparison shows your estimated amount alongside actual costs calculated from recorded time and cost rates. It helps you gauge whether a matter is on track financially or heading over its fee estimate.

lifecycle.title: Fee note lifecycle
lifecycle.body: Fee notes start as drafts, where you can edit line items and details. Once sent to a client, a fee note is locked. It then moves to paid when payment is received, or marked overdue if payment is late. Only draft fee notes can be modified.

unbilledTime.title: Unbilled time
unbilledTime.body: Unbilled time recordings are hours recorded against tasks that have not yet been included on a fee note. Use the fee note generator to pull unbilled time into a new fee note for a specific client and date range.

numbering.title: Fee note numbering
numbering.body: Fee note numbers are generated sequentially (e.g., INV-0001, INV-0002). The format uses a prefix followed by a zero-padded counter that increments automatically. This ensures every fee note has a unique, sortable reference.

variables.title: Template variables
variables.body: Use {{variable}} syntax in your templates to insert dynamic data. When a document is generated, variables like {{project.name}}, {{customer.name}}, and {{invoice.total}} are replaced with real values from your matter, client, or fee note.

tiptapVsWord.title: Tiptap vs. Word templates
tiptapVsWord.body: Tiptap templates are rich-text templates edited directly in your browser with a visual editor. Word (.docx) templates are uploaded files that use mail-merge style placeholders. Choose Tiptap for simple documents and Word for complex formatting needs.

packs.title: Template packs
packs.body: Template packs are pre-built collections of common document types — engagement letters, fee notes, letters of demand. Clone a pack to get started quickly, then customise the templates to match your organisation's branding and terminology.

types.title: Field types
types.body: Choose from text, number, date, single-select, or multi-select field types. Text fields capture free-form input. Number and date fields validate their format. Select fields let you define a list of options to choose from.

scoping.title: Field scoping
scoping.body: Custom fields can be scoped to matters, clients, or tasks. A matter-scoped field appears on all matters but not on clients or tasks. This keeps forms focused and avoids irrelevant fields cluttering your data entry.

utilisation.title: Utilisation rate
utilisation.body: Utilisation measures the percentage of total tracked time that is billable. A higher rate means more of your team's effort is generating revenue. Industry benchmarks typically range from 60% to 80%.

projectHealth.title: Matter health
projectHealth.body: Matter health combines fee estimate usage, timeline progress, and task completion into an overall status indicator. It provides a quick visual signal to help you identify matters that may need attention.

profitability.title: Profitability margin
profitability.body: Profitability is calculated as revenue (from billing rates) minus cost (from cost rates), shown as a percentage. It tells you how much margin you're earning on each matter, client, or across the organisation.

saved.title: Saved views
saved.body: Save your current filter, sort, and column configuration as a named view. Switch between views to see your data from different angles — for example, a view for active matters only, or tasks due this week.

overview.title: Tags
overview.body: Tags are colour-coded labels you can attach to matters, tasks, and clients. Use them to categorise work by type, priority, department, or any system that fits your workflow. Items can have multiple tags.

preferences.title: Notification preferences
preferences.body: Control which events trigger notifications and how you receive them. For each event type — such as task assignments, comments, or fee estimate alerts — choose between in-app notifications, email, or both.

overview.title: Team management
overview.body: Invite members, assign roles, and manage permissions for your organization.

general.title: Organization settings
general.body: Configure your organization's currency, tax, and branding.

overview.title: Integrations
overview.body: Connect third-party tools like accounting software, payment gateways, and email providers.

overview.title: Billing
overview.body: View your billing method and subscription status. Billing is managed by your administrator.

setup.title: Getting started
setup.body: Follow the setup checklist to configure your organization and start managing matters.

contacts.title: Portal contacts
contacts.body: Portal contacts are external users who can access the client portal to view documents, respond to requests, and accept engagement letters.
